Time-varying effects in model formulas

Source: R/temporal.R
tv.Rd

tv() lets the effect of a variable change over time (temporal instability). Used in a model formula, tv(x, time = year) replaces the single coefficient of x by one effect for each value of year, parameterized by a basis chosen for the question being asked. It can be used in the mean formula and in the formulas of distribution parameters, zero models and the other auxiliary formulas of every estimator, and tv(1, time = year) gives a time-varying intercept.

Usage

tv(
  x,
  time,
  basis = c("step", "level", "hinge", "smooth"),
  levels = NULL,
  new_time = c("error", "nearest"),
  ...
)

Arguments

x

the numeric variable whose effect varies, or 1 for the intercept.

time

the time variable (numeric, such as a year, or a factor). Its distinct values in the estimation data define the periods, in increasing order (factor level order for a factor).

basis

how the period effects \(\beta_t\) are parameterized:

"step" (default)

the effect in the first period and the change at each later period: \(\beta_t = \beta_1 + \sum_{k=2}^t \Delta_k\). A zero change \(\Delta_k\) means equal effects in periods \(k-1\) and \(k\). Columns x:time<first> and x:time_step<k>.

"level"

a separate effect for each period (columns x:time<t>). A zero coefficient means no effect in that period.

"hinge"

the cumulative "spline indicators" of Shabab et al. (2026): \(\beta_t = \sum_k \max(t - k + 1, 0)\,\delta_k\), with \(t\) the period's position (1, 2, ...). A zero \(\delta_k\) means that the trend of the earlier periods continues at period \(k\), not that the effect stays the same: dropping \(\delta_2\) imposes \(\beta_2 = 2\beta_1\). Columns x:time_hinge<k>.

"smooth"

a penalized spline in time, \(\beta(t)\), the varying-coefficient smooth s(time, by = x) of mgcv, so the data choose between a constant, a linear trend and a flexible path. time must be numeric. Arguments in ... (such as k and bs) are passed to mgcv::s(); k defaults to the number of periods, at most 10.

The step, level and hinge bases give the same fit (the same log-likelihood) and the same period effects; they differ in what the individual coefficients and their tests mean.

levels

the periods. Set from the estimation data; give it only to fix the periods in advance.

new_time

what to do at prediction for a time value that was not in the estimation data: "error" (default), or "nearest" to use the effect of the nearest period (numeric time only), for example the last period's effect for a later year.

...

arguments passed to mgcv::s() with basis = "smooth".

Value

A numeric matrix with one column per basis function (it is meant to be used inside a model formula).

Details

With an intercept in the model, tv(1, time = year) leaves out its first column: the intercept is the first period's level, and the remaining columns are the changes ("step"), the differences from the first period ("level") or the hinge terms from the second period ("hinge"). A variable should appear either alone or in tv(), not both.

Use temporal_effects() for the effect in each period with its standard error, and temporal_tests() to test whether and when the effects change.

References

Shabab, K. R., Bhowmik, T., Zaki, M. H. and Eluru, N. (2026). A joint count and generalized ordered fractional split approach for addressing temporal instability in road safety analysis. Analytic Methods in Accident Research, 51, 100440.

See also

temporal_effects(), temporal_tests()

Examples

data("washington_roads")
m <- countreg(Total_crashes ~ tv(lnaadt, time = Year) + speed50 +
                offset(lnlength), data = washington_roads,
              family = "NB2", method = "BFGS")
temporal_effects(m)
#>   part   term time basis period estimate  std.error conf.low conf.high
#> 1 mean lnaadt Year  step   2016 1.130270 0.05200214 1.028348  1.232193
#> 2 mean lnaadt Year  step   2017 1.123700 0.05201507 1.021752  1.225648
#> 3 mean lnaadt Year  step   2018 1.120515 0.05185510 1.018881  1.222149
temporal_tests(m)
#>   part   term         test    estimate  std.error  statistic df   p.value
#> 1 mean lnaadt    all equal          NA         NA  0.5951265  2 0.7426256
#> 2 mean lnaadt 2017 vs 2016 -0.00657049 0.01297047 -0.5065731  1 0.6124544
#> 3 mean lnaadt 2018 vs 2017 -0.00318521 0.01308643 -0.2433979  1 0.8076972
